title: Safely managed drinking water, Northern Africa and Western Asia, by location
headline: In N. Africa and W. Asia, safely managed water for all by 2030 needs a rise of 4.0 points a year
subtitle: Proportion of the population using drinking water from an improved source that is accessible on premises, available when needed and free from contamination
years: So far it has risen 0.4 points a year, from 66.5% in 2000 to 76.2% in 2024.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_H2O_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: In N. Africa and W. Asia, safely managed water for all by 2030 needs a rise of 4.0 points a year. So far it has risen 0.4 points a year, from 66.5% in 2000 to 76.2% in 2024. People using safely managed drinking water, Northern Africa and Western Asia: 66.5% in 2000, 76.2% in 2024. At that pace about 78.6% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 4.0 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has safely managed drinking water moved at anything like 4.0 points a year, and what made it possible?
